entries.title: I Samuel 25:1
segments:
At Ramah; the place where he was born, and had lived. 
 
  Paran; near the southern border of Judah. 
 
The removal by death of the wise and good is a just cause of lamentation to the living, and should lead to fervent prayer that God would raise up others to fill their places, and carry forward his work.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:2
segments: Carmel; a few miles south of Hebron.  It should be distinguished from mount Carmel on the Mediterranean.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:6
segments: Kind feelings manifested in kind words and actins, even towards the evil and unthankful, are means of great good to those who indulge them, and tend to the good of all who feel their influence.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:8
segments: Whatsoever cometh to thy hand; what he had and could conveniently spare.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:10
segments: Unkindness and reproaches torment those who indulge in them, and often tempt others to commit sin.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:14
segments: Servants are often wiser and better than their masters, are more grateful for kindness, and more disposed to treat it as it deserves.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:16
segments: A wall unto us; they protected us.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:18
segments: A prudent wife is from the Lord, and may be the means in his hands of unspeakable good to her husband.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:22
segments:
So and more also do God; this was a kind of oath which David took that he would destroy every man belonging to Nabal. 
 
Men who have nobly withstood great and sore temptations, may meanly give way to those which are small, and profanely resolve to commit such enormous crimes as would cover them with deserved and perpetual disgrace.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:24
segments:
This iniquity; the blame belonging to her husband for so basely treating David and his men. 
 
  Audience; hearing

entries.title: I Samuel 25:25
segments: Nabal; meaning folly.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:26
segments:
Hath withholden thee; by sending Abigail to persuade him not to do as he had intended. 
 
All the wisdom needful in conducting a difficult concern, and all the success of human efforts in accomplishing it, come from God, and to him the wise and the good will give the glory.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:27
segments: This blessing; the present she had brought.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:28
segments: Make my lord a sure house; establish and prosper him in his kingdom.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:29
segments:
A man; Saul. 
 
  Soul; life. 
 
  Bound in the bundle; surely be preserved. 
 
  Sling out; destroy or reject them.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:30
segments: When one is raised by God to a station of great power and influence, it is a source of much pleasure to be able to look back and see that he has not swerved from the path of truth and duty in order to obtain it.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:32
segments: However great the blessings which come through the instrumentality of creatures, we should not overlook the Creator, or fail to acknowledge his gracious agency in the affairs of men; nor while we acknowledge him as the source of all good, should we fail to be grateful to the voluntary and benevolent instruments through which his goodness is bestowed.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:34
segments: None but God knows how many evils may be averted from a foolish and wicked husband by a pious, prudent, and energetic wife.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:36
segments: A person when drunk is ordinarily not in a condition to be benefited by conversation, and it is not usually wise, while he is in that state, to attempt to converse with him.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:37
segments: His heart died; he was overcome and became senseless.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:38
segments: Many a drunkard, after lying for a time as dead, has been smitten by the Lord, and in less than ten days has gone to the drunkard's grave; and no one who falls into the drunkard's sleep can avoid the danger of awaking in the drunkard's eternity.

entries.title: I Samuel 25:43
segments: Men who see and acknowledge the duty and the blessedness of obeying God, and in some things actually do it; in other things, when tempted, are sometimes left openly to rebel against him, and thus pierce themselves and others through with many sorrows.
